title: CiteSeerX (identifier)
summary: CiteSeerX is a closed-down public search engine and digital library for scientific papers, primarily in computer and information science, that harvested freely available documents from author websites using automated metadata extraction and focused crawling. It expanded beyond its predecessor by supporting broader scholarly domains and offered its metadata under a Creative Commons license for non-commercial reuse. The system relied on open-source infrastructure, Apache Solr, and machine learning tools to extract titles, authors, abstracts, and citation contexts, though its coverage was limited to publicly accessible papers and it returned fewer citation counts than services with publisher metadata access. In 2026, the service shut down due to lack of funding, with remaining links redirecting to the Internet Archive.

mechanisms.title: Focused crawling and automated metadata extraction
mechanisms.explanation: CiteSeerX used automated information extraction tools, typically machine learning-based, to pull scholarly metadata such as title, authors, abstract, and citations from publicly available documents, primarily author webpages. It employed focused crawling to harvest these open resources, but could not access publisher metadata, resulting in lower citation counts compared to services like Google Scholar.

mechanisms.title: Open data sharing via Creative Commons license
mechanisms.explanation: CiteSeerX shared its metadata, databases, and software under a Creative Commons BY-NC-SA license, enabling researchers worldwide to reuse the data in experiments and competitions. The system also provided an OAI-PMH endpoint, making its content indexable by academic search engines and institutional repositories.
